span.p: Derive the key once, then persist it on the queue row

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
v1:{domain}:{entity}:{id}:{occurrence}
Never an execution id, never a timestamp,
never an attempt counter. Retries read the key
back off the queue row rather than recomputing
it, so drifting inputs cannot mint a new key.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: One statement, leasing the work and reading any existing claim

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING,
alongside a SELECT of the existing row. The
insert says whether we won; the select is how
the Observed guards below have state to read.

span.p: dead_letter row, keeping the original key

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Idempotent by construction: every later attempt
lands in Observed and short-circuits there.
Case 8 is proven from outside, by asserting the
provider journal recorded exactly one delivery.
